The main chat model is the coordinator. It decomposes, dispatches, accepts and summarizes — it should not do all the work itself. Independent tasks run in parallel; dependent phases wait for acceptance. Sub-agent turn budget is assigned by the coordinator per task (simple ≈ 10, complex 40–60) with a fixed 200-turn runaway guard, and is not user-adjustable.

One row per concurrent teammate (linked to the cap of %1$d). Pick a model for each sub-agent, or leave it on the main session model. The N-th parallel spawn_agent member uses sub-agent N. A call may still name a model.

Privileged Android control via Shizuku or AXManager

Shizuku exposes privileged system APIs to user apps without root, by running a small service started via wireless ADB or root. Three compatible providers are supported — Shizuku (RikkaApps), AXManager (Axeron), and Sui (a Magisk/KernelSU module for rooted devices); install any one. Once authorized, Minis Ultra can use the android-shizuku-cli CLI for package, permission, settings, input, and activity management.
Run `android-shizuku-cli --help` in a shell for full usage. Available whether the binder comes from Shizuku, AXManager, or Sui — the command surface is identical.

Install any one of Shizuku (RikkaApps), AXManager (Axeron), or Sui (RikkaApps) — all three implement the same protocol and are fully interchangeable. Shizuku and AXManager are regular apps activated via wireless ADB. Sui is for already-rooted devices: it installs as a Magisk/KernelSU module, needs no app, and stays active across reboots. On KernelSU or APatch, Sui also requires a Zygisk implementation (Zygisk Next / ReZygisk / NeoZygisk) — without it Sui will not load. Install one, then return here.

Open the manager app and start the service via wireless ADB (no PC) or root. After it shows running, return here.\n\nUsing AXManager? Also enable Settings → "AX-Permission Intercept" inside AXManager — only that switch makes AXManager push its Shizuku-compatible binder to Minis Ultra.
